module_title: Newton's Laws of Motion, Momentum, and Friction
introduction: While kinematics studies 'how' things move, Dynamics studies 'why' they move. Sir Isaac Newton formulated three universal laws that relate forces to motion, explaining everything from falling apples to rocket launches.

core_concepts.title: Newton's First Law (Law of Inertia)
core_concepts.description:
An object at rest stays at rest, and an object in motion stays in uniform motion, unless acted upon by an external unbalanced force. 
'Inertia' is the inherent property of a body to resist any change in its state. (e.g., When a bus starts suddenly, passengers fall backward due to inertia of rest).

core_concepts.title: Newton's Second Law (Law of Momentum)
core_concepts.description:
The rate of change of momentum of a body is directly proportional to the applied force. 
Momentum ($p$) = Mass $\times$ Velocity. 
This law gives the famous formula: Force = Mass $\times$ Acceleration ($F = ma$). It provides the 'measurement' of force.

core_concepts.title: Newton's Third Law (Action and Reaction)
core_concepts.description:
For every action, there is an equal and opposite reaction. 
Examples: The recoil of a gun when a bullet is fired, a swimmer pushing water backward to move forward, and the propulsion of a rocket (expelling gases downward to push the rocket upward).

core_concepts.title: Friction (The Opposing Force)
core_concepts.description:
A force that opposes relative motion between two surfaces in contact. 
1. Static Friction: Force required to start moving a resting object (Highest). 
2. Kinetic Friction: Force opposing an already moving object. 
3. Rolling Friction: Opposes rolling motion (Lowest, which is why wheels were invented).

important_entities.name: Conservation of Linear Momentum
important_entities.significance: If no external force acts on a system, its total momentum remains conserved. This is the underlying principle behind rocket propulsion and collisions. (Total momentum before firing = Total momentum after firing).

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.alert_title: Action and Reaction DO NOT Cancel Out
trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Exam Trap: 'If action and reaction are equal and opposite, why don't they cancel each other and result in zero net force?' Answer: Because action and reaction forces always act on 'TWO DIFFERENT BODIES'. They only cancel out if they act on the same body.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: The 1st law defines what force is (it breaks inertia). The 2nd law gives the formula to measure it ($F=ma$). The 3rd law explains how forces interact in pairs.

exam_strategy_tips: In SSC exams, 'Catching a cricket ball by pulling hands backward' is a classic question. This is an application of Newton's Second Law (increasing time reduces the rate of change of momentum, thus reducing the force on the hands).
